accepted_interpretation.interpretation: Random matrix theory is used as a conjecture-generating cross-domain dictionary, not a certificate. Wigner's earlier proposal treated random matrices as a statistical surrogate for poorly understood nuclear energy levels; analogously, Dyson observed that Montgomery's pair-correlation distribution appeared to match that of random Hermitian eigenvalues. For zeta moments, modelling zeros up to height T by matrices of dimension near log(T/(2π)) produces conjectural values of the integer factor f(k) for all k, consistent with earlier analytic results and independently conjectured values and corroborated numerically. The dictionary gains tractable matrix problems but lacks a general proof that its predictions transfer back.
